summary.title: What I Learned from Doing 60+ Technical Interviews in 30 Days
summary.one_liner: Uduak Obong-Eren's first-hand lessons from 60+ interviews in early 2020, covering applications, phone screens, coding challenges, take-home projects, on-site and virtual interviews, and handling failure.
takeaways: Treat each job application as a tailored sales pitch; quality over quantity, with a reported ratio of about 1 interview per 12 applications.
Communicate your thought process out loud in technical screens and when stuck, since interviewers evaluate collaboration as well as correctness.
For timed coding challenges, get working brute-force code first, then test edge cases and optimize.
Know multiple solutions and their trade-offs, write clean modular code, and only use tools you are comfortable with.
Practice with mock interviews and keep interviewing periodically to build confidence.
summary.summary:
The author describes a 30-day job search in January to March 2020 that produced more than 60 interviews from 109+ applications, including phone screens, take-home projects, coding challenges and on-site interviews. The article is organized by recruitment phase: pre-interview (applications and recruiter messages), the interview itself (phone calls, phone screens, coding challenges, take-homes, on-site and virtual), and after the interview (handling failure and success). It is a personal lessons-learned essay with anecdotes rather than a tutorial, and it ends with a list of external resources on interviewing.</summary>
